name: Scale AI
statusNote: Still independent and private as of Oct 2026. Meta bought a 49% NON-VOTING stake for $14.3B in June 2025, and founder Alexandr Wang left to join Meta. Because Meta has no voting control, Scale is treated as independent private rather than a subsidiary. Board named Francis deSouza (Google Cloud COO) CEO effective 2026-08-10, replacing interim CEO Jason Droege.
oneLiner: Training and evaluation data for frontier labs, plus AI applications for enterprises and governments.
founders: Alexandr Wang (left June 2025 to become Meta's Chief AI Officer; still on Scale's board) and Lucy Guo (left early). Current CEO is Francis deSouza (ex-Google Cloud COO, ex-Illumina CEO), effective Aug 10, 2026.
talentSignals: Founder/CEO Alexandr Wang departed to Meta with the June 2025 deal; Jason Droege served as interim CEO for over a year (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-30/scale-ai-names-google-cloud-executive-francis-desouza-as-new-ceo)

Roughly 200 employees and 500 contractors were laid off in July 2025 when the gen-AI data unit was restructured (reported via https://valueaddvc.com/blog/scale-ai-valuation-what-the-data-labeling-company-is-worth-after-the-meta-deal)
Permanent CEO is a big-company operator (Francis deSouza from Google Cloud), not a researcher (https://scale.com/blog/scale-appoints-new-ceo)
research: Runs evaluation and benchmark work, for example the SEAL leaderboards; no specifics were verified this pass. Its public output is mostly applied and product-oriented.
xPresence: @scale_AI has 81.2k followers. @alexandr_wang has 772.7k followers, but his bio now reads Meta chief AI officer, so his reach no longer really benefits Scale. No current Scale exec with a large following was found.
traction: Revenue was 'just shy of $1B' in 2025, up from $870M in 2024; Scale expects more than $1B in 2026 (Forbes, May 2026). Meta committed to at least $450M/yr for 5 years. 2025 bookings were over $1B. The applications business is about $200M annualized and expected to double in 2026 (https://scale.com/blog/scales-next-era-building-for-2026). New customers include BP and Mayo Clinic.
moat: Government/defense relationships, a guaranteed Meta contract, and a large existing labeling workforce and tooling.
risks: Other frontier labs (OpenAI, Google) pulled back after the Meta deal. Growth is slow next to Mercor/Surge, the business is concentrated on Meta, and the founder has left.
notes: Not an IPO or acquisition, but heavily dependent on Meta. No priced round or secondary since June 2025. Sacra estimates higher 2025 revenue ($2B); I used the company-to-Forbes figure. No verified X posts captured. Headcount not found.

name: Mercor
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026. Last announced priced round is the Oct 2025 Series C at $10B. A ~$20B round (General Catalyst leading, Nvidia discussed) was reported in Jul–Aug 2026 but its close has not been announced.
oneLiner: A marketplace that recruits and pays domain experts (30k+ weekly active) to make training and eval data for AI labs and enterprises.
founders: Brendan Foody (co-CEO), Adarsh Hiremath (co-CEO), Surya Midha (board chair). All three are Thiel Fellows, about 23 years old, and Forbes calls them the youngest self-made billionaires.
talentSignals: Forbes reported each founder would be worth about $4.3B if the $20B round closes (https://www.forbes.com/sites/richardnieva/2026/07/09/mercor-fundraise/)
Pays more than $2M/day to 30,000+ weekly active contractors (https://dealroom.co/news/137121-mercor-doubles-to-2b-gross-revenue-run-rate-as-ai-labs-buy-expert-data/)
Took over clients Scale AI lost after the Meta deal (https://valueaddvc.com/blog/how-does-mercor-make-money-2b-arr-20b-valuation-and-the-expert-data-marketplace-explained)
research: Little public research output was verified this pass.

xPosts.author: BrendanFoody
xPosts.summary: 'Mercor grew from $1M to $2B in ARR in 24 months... fastest growth trajectory in history'; says Enterprise is the fastest-growing segment.

xPresence: @BrendanFoody has 29.2k followers; the $2B ARR post passed 1M views. @mercor has 25.1k followers.
traction: Gross run rate went from $1B to $2B in four months (Feb to Jun 2026). Contractors receive 60–70% of that, so net revenue is about $600–800M. Free-cash-flow profitable. Gross revenue in H1 2026 was $614M (Sacra estimate). Nvidia paid Mercor tens of millions in one quarter for Nemotron data (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-reportedly-explores-stake-ai-204528438.html).
moat: Two-sided network of vetted experts plus deep relationships with the labs (OpenAI, Google DeepMind). Speed of matching.
risks: The $2B is gross, not net revenue. Customers are concentrated among a few labs. The labor-marketplace model has low switching costs, and contractor and legal disputes are possible.
notes: Trackers (LinkedIn data, revenuememo) mention Series D shares issued in Aug 2026, but the company has not announced the round's size, close, or valuation, so latestValuation stays at $10B. Headcount not found.

name: Turing
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. Its last disclosed round was the Mar 2025 Series E. It launched Turing Frontier in Apr 2026 and hired a CFO (Varsha Udayabhanu, ex-Invisible) in Aug 2026, which may point toward a raise or IPO preparation.
oneLiner: Coding, reasoning, and STEM training data from a 4M-person talent cloud for frontier labs, plus enterprise agentic-AI deployments.
founders: Jonathan Siddharth (CEO; former Quora board member; ex-Foundation Capital EIR; co-author of SpotSigs) and Vijay Krishnan (CTO).
talentSignals: OpenAI approached Turing in 2022 for code data, which seeded its frontier-data business (https://techcrunch.com/2025/03/06/turing-a-key-coding-provider-for-openai-and-other-llm-producers-raises-111m-at-a-2-2b-valuation/)
Hired CFO Varsha Udayabhanu, ex-CFO of Invisible Technologies, in Aug 2026 (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jonsid_the-best-ai-companies-have-to-move-at-breakneck-activity-7497685463067996160-WTK1)
research: Its 'Turing Research' arm builds coding, math, multimodal, and industry benchmarks. It also has the ALAN fine-tuning/RL platform. No major paper output was verified.
xPresence: No company or CEO X handle could be confirmed via fxtwitter (@turingcom and @jonsidd return 404). Effectively a quiet presence on X.
traction: About $300M ARR in early 2025, roughly 3x year over year, and profitable for about a year at that point. Customers include OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Amazon (per Sourcery interview). Launched Turing Frontier (US-based expert network) in Apr 2026. No 2026 revenue figure was found.
moat: A 4M+ developer talent cloud and long-standing relationships with the labs.
risks: Commoditized human-data market with fierce competition (Mercor, Surge, Scale, Snorkel). No public revenue update since early 2025.
notes: TechCrunch says the Series E 'doubled' the valuation from $1.1B. Total raised was $225M as of Mar 2025. No 2026 round, ARR, or headcount was found.

name: Snorkel AI
statusNote: Private; raised a $350M Series E at $3.5B on 2026-09-22.
oneLiner: A 'frontier AI data lab' that builds expert data, RL environments, and evals for frontier labs and enterprises, spun out of Stanford's programmatic-labeling research.
founders: Alex Ratner (CEO; Stanford PhD under Chris Ré; UW affiliate assistant professor), with co-founders from the Stanford AI Lab Snorkel project, including Chris Ré, Paroma Varma, Braden Hancock, and Henry Ehrenberg.
talentSignals: Grew out of the Stanford AI Lab; the team pioneered data-centric AI (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/snorkel-ai-raises-350m-to-scale-the-data-factory-for-frontier-ai-302886796.html)
250+ peer-reviewed papers with 25,000+ citations, per the company (same source)
research: Long academic track record (the Snorkel OSS project, weak supervision, data-centric AI); 250+ peer-reviewed papers and 25k+ citations by company count. It runs an Open Benchmarks Grants program.

xPosts.author: ajratner
xPosts.summary: CEO announces the $350M Series E at $3.5B; says the company grew 18x+ in 12 months since launching Data-as-a-Service and passed $375M ARR.

xPosts.author: SnorkelAI
xPosts.summary: Company account announces the $350M at $3.5B and the $375M ARR milestone.

xPresence: @SnorkelAI has 18.2k followers and @ajratner 7.3k. Launch posts reach tens of thousands of views.
traction: ARR grew 18x+ in about 12 months after Expert Data-as-a-Service launched in Sept 2025, reaching ~$350M (Reuters) to $375M (CEO). Expects to be profitable in 2026 (Reuters). Works with leading labs and enterprises (BNY, QBE, and Wells Fargo are investors and customers).
moat: Combines research credibility with a programmatic data platform; it also has an enterprise footprint.
risks: Revenue swung sharply toward lab data services, which are lumpy and concentrated, in a crowded field.
notes: Reuters puts the run rate at ~$350M while the CEO's tweet says $375M; I used the tweet for the headline and recorded both. Headcount not found.

name: Datacurve
statusNote: Private and VC-backed (YC W24). Series A in Oct 2025; no later round found.
oneLiner: Frontier coding training data, sourced through Shipd, a gamified bounty platform for skilled software engineers.
founders: Serena Ge (CEO; Waterloo CS dropout at 18; previously worked with Cohere's CTO on reasoning/coding synthetic data) and Charley Lee (ex-Google intern). Both were about 19 at founding.
talentSignals: Series A angels include employees of DeepMind, Vercel, Anthropic, and OpenAI (https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/09/datacurve-raises-15-million-to-take-on-scaleai/)
YC lists a team size of 25 (https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/datacurve)
research: Private coding benchmarks used to target model weaknesses; no notable public papers found.
xPresence: @datacurve has 11.1k followers. No CEO handle was confirmed.
traction: Over $1M paid out in bounties by Oct 2025, with multimillion-dollar contracts at leading labs and a large seven-figure deal (https://www.chemistry.vc/post/staying-ahead-of-the-curve). Shipd has 14k+ vetted engineers (Sacra).
moat: A community of engineers attracted by gamified bounties; thin moat.
risks: Small player against Mercor, Turing, and Surge in coding data, and dependent on a few lab customers.
notes: Valuation not disclosed. Revenue figures exist only from aggregators (LinkedIn data ~$4.5M; GetLatka ~$2.9M for 2024), are unreliable, and were not used. No 2026 funding news found.

name: Bespoke Labs
oneLiner: A research lab building RL environments and post-training data infrastructure for reliable long-horizon agents.
founders: Mahesh Sathiamoorthy (CEO; nearly a decade at Google/DeepMind; invented Generative Retrieval/TIGER, NeurIPS 2023; KDD best paper) and Alex Dimakis (Chief Scientist; UC Berkeley professor, IEEE Fellow, 150+ papers, DataComp).
talentSignals: Jeff Dean was a seed investor, and angels came from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta (https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260706827813/bespoke-labs-announces-40m-to-build-the-environments-that-train-reliable-agents)
Wing VC's thesis piece on the founders' pedigree (https://www.wing.vc/content/investing-in-bespoke-ai)
research: Strong open research for its size. It co-leads OpenThoughts (open reasoning dataset; paper at ICLR), contributes to Terminal-Bench and GEPA, built Bespoke-Stratos, and released Bespoke Curator, an OSS synthetic-data curation tool.
traction: Early commercial work, including a production deployment at Intuit Credit Karma (per AI Engineer talk). Serves frontier labs and enterprises with environments. No revenue disclosed.
moat: Research credibility and the open-source community (OpenThoughts) give it trust with labs.
risks: Crowded RL-environment market; small and early revenue.
notes: Wing's blog says the Series A was $31.3M and the seed $8.25M (total about $40M). Valuation, revenue, and headcount not disclosed.

name: Collinear AI
statusNote: Private, seed-stage. No priced round has been publicly announced. Aggregators (Caplight) report about $10M raised.
oneLiner: 'AI Simulation Lab' that builds sandboxed RL environments, verifiers, and training/eval data for agents.
founders: Nazneen Rajani (CEO; formerly led post-training/robustness research at Hugging Face; Salesforce Research; UT Austin PhD; MIT TR 35 Under 35; UN AI Advisory Body) and Soumyadeep Bakshi.
talentSignals: The CEO's Hugging Face and Salesforce Research pedigree (https://www.rl-list.com/vendors/collinear)
research: Builds security/coding benchmarks (a CWE-based benchmark that Artificial Analysis reportedly uses in its Cyber Index, per the rl-list profile; not independently verified) and the SimLab tooling.
traction: No disclosed revenue or customers verified.
moat: Thin; it is an environment and verifier vendor in a crowded space.
risks: Under-capitalized compared with peers; funding is undisclosed.
notes: Investors include Engineering Capital, 11.2 Capital, B Capital, Storm Ventures, and Hitachi Ventures (company About page via rl-list). The ~$10M funding figure comes only from an aggregator. Headcount (30) is aggregator-sourced.

name: Haize Labs
statusNote: Acquired by Beacon Software (a Toronto AI holding company) on 2026-09-17; terms undisclosed. The team became Beacon's Applied AI Research Group, and CEO Leonard Tang became VP of AI Research.
oneLiner: Red-teaming, guardrails, evals, and observability for AI agents (before its acquisition).
founders: Leonard Tang (CEO; Harvard; Stanford PhD dropout; ex-BAIR undergrad researcher), Richard Liu, and Steve Li (Harvard, BAIR).
talentSignals: Young Harvard team; $100M valuation within its first year (https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/general-catalyst-haize-labs-100-million-valuation)
research: Red-teaming and jailbreak research; the CEO co-authored a PNAS 2021 paper on math-solving neural networks.
traction: Customers included Anthropic, OpenAI, Air Canada, Deloitte, and Epic Games (https://betakit.com/beacon-buys-new-yorks-haize-labs-to-boost-ai-reliability-across-its-portfolio/).
moat: Small; acquired as an acqui-hire-style deal.
notes: EXCLUDE from the private ranking: acquired by Beacon in Sept 2026. LP Club reports $7.45M total raised and a Dec 2024 $7M SAFE at $100M post. PitchBook dates the GC-led $100M valuation to Aug 2024.

name: Goodfire
statusNote: Private public benefit corporation; Series B in Feb 2026.
oneLiner: Interpretability research lab building tools to understand, debug, and intentionally design models (Ember, then the Silico platform).
founders: Eric Ho (CEO; previously founded RippleMatch), Dan Balsam (CTO), and Tom McGrath (Chief Scientist; ex-Google DeepMind interpretability lead).
talentSignals: Team includes researchers who 'shaped modern neural network interpretability at OpenAI, DeepMind, Stanford, and Harvard' (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ai-lab-goodfire-raises-150m-at-1-25b-valuation-to-design-models-with-interpretability-302680120.html)
Staff include Nick Cammarata (started OpenAI's interpretability team with Chris Olah) and Lee Sharkey (https://www.longtermwiki.com/wiki/E430)
Anthropic made its first-ever direct startup investment in Goodfire's Series A (https://menlovc.com/perspective/leading-goodfires-50m-series-a-to-interpret-how-ai-models-think/)
research: Prolific interpretability research: interpreting Arc Institute's Evo 2, Alzheimer's biomarker discovery with Prima Mente ('first major natural-science finding from reverse-engineering a foundation model'), reward-hacking activation monitors (Sept 2026, tested on Kimi K3), RLFR (probes as RL rewards), and SAE educational series. Released the Silico platform publicly in Aug 2026.

xPosts.author: GoodfireAI
xPosts.summary: Thread: 'Models know when they're reward hacking' in 50–96% of rollouts studied; activation monitors detect it in real time.

xPresence: @GoodfireAI has 27.6k followers; research threads reach 100k+ views. CEO handle not confirmed.
traction: Partners include Arc Institute, Mayo Clinic, Microsoft, Rakuten, and Prima Mente. Silico platform launched publicly Aug 2026. No revenue disclosed.
moat: A rare concentration of interpretability talent plus a research brand.
risks: Commercial model is unproven, and big labs (Anthropic, DeepMind) do interpretability in-house.
notes: Over $200M raised in total. Revenue and headcount not found. Chris Olah is NOT at Goodfire (still at Anthropic).

name: HUMAN Security
statusNote: Private and PE/growth-backed (Goldman Sachs Merchant Banking-led deal in 2020; $50M+ growth round led by WestCap in Oct 2024). No IPO or acquisition as of Oct 2026. Identity: this is the bot/fraud-defense HUMAN, as the brief specified. CAUTION: if the list intended an AI startup, it may have meant 'humans&' (Redwood City AI lab; $480M seed at $4.48B in Jan 2026, https://www.reuters.com/business/ai-startup-humans-raises-480-million-45-billion-valuation-seed-round-2026-01-20/), which was NOT researched here.
oneLiner: Bot, fraud, and 'agentic trust' defense that verifies whether traffic comes from humans, bots, or AI agents across ads, apps, and accounts.
founders: Founded as White Ops by Michael Tiffany, Tamer Hassan, and Ash Kalb (Tracxn lists Jay Crystal instead of Hassan). CEO is Stu Solomon.
research: Threat-intelligence reports, for example the 2026 State of AI Traffic & Cyberthreat Benchmark, which found AI-agent traffic up 7,851% year over year.
xPresence: No company X handle was confirmed via fxtwitter. Effectively no presence.
traction: Analyzes over a quadrillion interactions a year and serves 500+ brands (2024). Repositioned around 'Agentic Trust' in 2026, with channel partnerships (Nuaware, Confused.com, Sept 2026).
moat: Large behavioral signal network and established ad-fraud and enterprise customer base.
risks: Not an AI-native startup. Mature, PE-style company with flat headcount, competing with Cloudflare and Akamai bot management.
notes: Likely an outlier or mismatch for an 'AI startups' ranking; consider replacing with humans& if that was intended. Revenue (~$100M) and headcount (~520) come only from aggregators (LinkedIn data/Prospeo), so arr is left null. Total funding ~$299M (Tracxn).

name: Doppel
statusNote: Private. Series C in Nov 2025 at >$600M; MUFG Innovation Partners made a strategic late-stage investment in Sept 2026 (undisclosed).
oneLiner: AI-native social engineering defense: detects and takes down AI impersonation, phishing, and deepfake fraud, plus human-risk training and email security.
founders: Kevin Tian (CEO; ex-Uber senior engineer, ex-Lyft staff engineer/EM; Georgetown) and Rahul Madduluri (CTO; ex-Uber ML infrastructure).
talentSignals: Hired 60+ people in Q1 2026, bringing headcount above 200 (https://www.doppel.com/company/press-releases/doppel-enters-japan-marking-next-phase-global-expansion)
Built detection agents with OpenAI (https://www.securityweek.com/doppel-banks-35m-for-ai-based-digital-risk-protection/)
xPresence: @DoppelHQ has 3.8k followers. Founders' handles not confirmed. Quiet.
traction: ARR grew more than 3x year over year and Fortune 500 customers grew 5x (June 2026). Passed 300 customers and had a record Q2 2026 for new enterprise customers. Expanded to Japan (June 2026) and EMEA (Oct 2025). (https://www.doppel.com/company/press-releases/mufg-innovation-partners-becomes-strategic-investor-doppel)
moat: Threat graph data and takedown automation; some enterprise lock-in.
risks: Crowded digital-risk-protection and security-awareness markets (ZeroFox, KnowBe4, Abnormal); absolute ARR is undisclosed.
notes: Series C valuation is 'over $600M' (recorded as 0.6). Total raised $124M after the Series C. PitchBook shows ~403 employees (aggregator). The MUFG round amount and valuation are undisclosed.

name: Hugging Face
statusNote: Nvidia signed a definitive agreement on 2026-09-02 (announced 2026-09-03) to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93B: about $11.9B to stockholders plus up to about $1.0B in retention equity. Closing is expected in H1 2027, pending regulatory approval, so it is technically still independent until then.
oneLiner: The hub for open models, datasets, and apps (3M models, 18M+ developers), plus inference and enterprise offerings.
founders: Clément Delangue (CEO), Julien Chaumond (CTO), Thomas Wolf (CSO).
talentSignals: Founders and team are staying on after the acquisition (https://x.com/ClementDelangue/status/2095482998674112733)
Deep open-source research bench (Transformers, SmolLM, open-r1); no specifics verified this pass
research: Major open-source infrastructure: the Transformers, Diffusers, and Datasets libraries and the Hub itself, plus open models and science projects. Among the most widely used OSS in AI.

xPosts.author: ClementDelangue
xPosts.summary: Announces 'our intention to join forces with NVIDIA in a $12,930,300,000 acquisition'; platform to stay open and compute-agnostic, founders staying.

xPosts.author: JensenHuang

xPresence: @huggingface 813.5k followers; @ClementDelangue 723.3k and frequently viral (the acquisition post passed 1.5M views).
traction: 18M individual users and 200k enterprise clients (per Nvidia, via Fortune). Hosts 3M models, 1M apps, and 500k datasets. Annualized revenue was about $150M in Aug 2026 (The Information via TechCrunch), up from about $81M at end-2025 (Sacra estimate).
compute: Will gain Nvidia's resources after the acquisition closes.
moat: Network effects as the default distribution hub for open models.
risks: Regulatory review of the Nvidia deal, neutrality concerns, and revenue that is small relative to usage.
notes: EXCLUDE or flag in the private ranking: pending acquisition by Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). Revenue figures are estimates from The Information and Sacra, not company-reported.

name: Ai2
statusNote: 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by Paul Allen. CEO Ali Farhadi stepped down in March 2026; Peter Clark is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent one.
oneLiner: Nonprofit lab building fully open models (OLMo, Molmo, Tülu) along with their data, code, and training recipes.
founders: Founded by Paul G. Allen; founding CEO Oren Etzioni. Key researchers include Noah Smith and Hanna Hajishirzi (OLMo leads).
talentSignals: At least 10 staff, including the core of the OLMo team (e.g., Luca Soldaini, Kyle Lo), left for Microsoft's Superintelligence team in 2026 (https://www.geekwire.com/2026/microsoft-adds-more-former-ai2-researchers-to-its-superintelligence-team/)
Iz Beltagy, an original OLMo member, returned as research lead (https://allenai.org/blog/omai-compute-now-live)
Primary funder (the Fund for Science and Technology) moved to proposal-based funding, which contributed to the exits (GeekWire)
research: Top-tier open research: OLMo 3 / 3.1 (fully open 7B–32B, Nov–Dec 2025), Molmo 2, Tülu, Olmo-core 3 (open MoE training stack scaling toward trillion parameters, Oct 1, 2026), and many top-venue papers.
xPresence: @allen_ai has 86.7k followers; model launches get meaningful reach.
traction: Research nonprofit, so no revenue. The NSF OMAI Blackwell Ultra cluster went live in May 2026.
compute: NSF OMAI cluster on Nvidia Blackwell Ultra ($152M NSF + Nvidia program).
moat: Credibility for full openness and backing from the Allen estate; not commercial.
risks: Attrition of OLMo leadership to Microsoft, CEO vacancy, and changing funding model.
notes: Nonprofit, so it is likely excluded from a private-startup valuation ranking. No valuation applies.

name: Superpower
statusNote: Private and VC-backed. The last announced round is the Apr 2025 Series A; trackers hint at a mid-2026 round (Caplight lists 'Series B Jun 2026', CB Insights an angel round on 2026-06-30), but none has been announced.
oneLiner: Consumer health 'super-app': 100+ biomarker lab tests, an AI health advisor, and concierge physicians, from $199 a year.
founders: Max Marchione (CEO; Sydney uni dropout, ex-Goldman Sachs IB), Jacob Peters, and Kevin Unkrich.
talentSignals: CEO claims '15 former founders, 3 ex-YC founders, Thiel fellow' on the team (https://www.forbes.com.au/news/entrepreneurs/sydney-uni-dropout-behind-432m-startup-teams-up-with-beckham-to-outsmart-aging/)
Team grew from 5 to 80 in two years (CEO LinkedIn post, June 2026)
xPresence: @maxmarchione 34.9k followers; @superpower 24.3k. The CEO credits Twitter/LinkedIn virality as a growth driver.
traction: CEO says 'tens of thousands of members and tens of millions in revenue', revenue up 100x and members up 600x in two years, and on track for $100M+ revenue within 12–18 months (https://www.withtitan.com/founders/max). Revenue grew 10x over the six months before Apr 2026 (Forbes Australia).
moat: Consumer brand and longitudinal health data; low barriers to entry (Function Health and others).
risks: Competition from Function Health; regulatory and clinical-claims risk; Forbes AU notes allegations against the company, which the CEO denies.
notes: Valuation is ambiguous. Forbes Australia (Apr 2026) says '$432M' valuation and a '$43M Series A', which look like AUD conversions of the USD 30M round. CB Insights shows $120M at the 2025 Series A. A Titan page says '>$500M in July 2026' without a primary source. All are left null. Membership price is $199/yr now (was $499 at launch).

name: Hippocratic AI
statusNote: Private. Last announced round was the Nov 2025 Series C at $3.5B. Its disclosed total funding rose from $404M to $444M by Aug 2026, implying about $40M of unannounced raises.
oneLiner: Safety-focused, non-diagnostic voice AI agents for health systems, payors, and pharma, built on its Polaris constellation model.
founders: Munjal Shah (CEO; previously founded Like.com, acquired by Google, and Health IQ) with clinical and technical co-founders.
talentSignals: Acquired Grove AI (clinical trials AI) in Jan 2026 and appointed a President of Life Sciences (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260112959357/en/Hippocratic-AI-Consolidates-Life-Sciences-Leadership-with-Acquisition-of-Grove-AI-and-Key-Executive-Appointments)
research: Polaris safety constellation architecture (patented, per the company); technical reports on Polaris. Moderate output.
traction: More than 250M patient voice interactions across 300+ live clinical use cases by Aug 2026, with about 280M by Oct 2026 (company LinkedIn). Works with nearly all of the top-10 US payors. Customers include Cleveland Clinic, Northwestern, and the NHS Guy's & St Thomas'. 50+ enterprise customers in 6 countries (Nov 2025).
moat: Clinical safety track record, health-system integrations, and the company taking contractual responsibility for its agents.
risks: Revenue undisclosed, slow healthcare procurement, and competition from Abridge, Ambience, and incumbents.
notes: No revenue figure from reliable reporting (LinkedIn data says $76M, an aggregator figure, not used). Leads for the seed, Series A, and Series B were not verified and are left null. The Series A ($53M, Mar 2024, ~$500M) and Series B ($141M, Jan 2025, $1.64B) amounts and valuations come from Fierce Healthcare and revenuememo.

name: Deel
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026. Series E in Oct 2025 at $17.3B. IPO has been discussed since 2025, but no filing or date has been announced.
oneLiner: Global HR, payroll, employer-of-record, and contractor payments platform for 37k+ businesses and 1.5M workers in 150+ countries.
founders: Alex Bouaziz (CEO) and Shuo Wang (CRO); YC W19.
traction: Passed $1.5B ARR in H1 2026, up from $1B in 2025. Profitable for three years. First $100M revenue month in Sept 2025. Processes $22B in payroll a year (Oct 2025).
moat: Owned payroll and legal-entity infrastructure in 100+ countries, compliance depth, and scale.
risks: Rippling litigation (trade-secret and espionage suits and countersuits). Secondary market prices it about 17% below the last round (Notice.co via Hustle Fund, mid-2026). Not an AI-native company.
notes: Not an AI startup, so it probably fits poorly in an AI ranking. Secondary-market implied valuation of about $14.3B (June 2026) is from Notice.co, an aggregator. Headcount not found.
